theory.intro: A **scalar** is a quantity with size only, such as a temperature of $18^{\circ}\text{C}$. A **vector** is a quantity with both a size and a direction, such as a wind of $30$ km/h from the south. The size of a vector is its **magnitude**.
facts: Mass, distance, speed, time, area and temperature are scalars, because a number and a unit describe each one fully.
Displacement, velocity, acceleration, force and weight are vectors, because each one also needs a direction.
The letters are read in travel order, so $\overrightarrow{AB}$ runs from $A$ to $B$ and $\overrightarrow{BA}$ runs the other way.
The magnitude of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ is written $|\underset{\sim}{a}|$, and the magnitude of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ is written $|\overrightarrow{AB}|$.
A magnitude is a length, so it is a scalar and is never negative.
A scalar may multiply a vector, as in $7\underset{\sim}{a}$, but a scalar can never be added to a vector.
steps: State the size and unit the quantity gives
Decide whether a direction is needed as well
Name it a vector if both are needed, or a scalar if the size alone is enough

foundation.question_text: A parcel has a mass of $4$ kg. State whether this is a vector or a scalar quantity, and give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
A mass of $4$ kg gives a size only, and no direction is attached to it.
It is a **scalar**.

foundation.question_text: A car travels at $80$ km/h on a bearing of $150^{\circ}$. State whether this is a vector or a scalar quantity, and give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
The quantity gives a size, $80$ km/h, and a direction, $150^{\circ}$.
It is a **vector**.

foundation.question_text: A hiker walks $12$ km along a winding track. State whether the quantity '$12$ km walked' is a vector or a scalar.
foundation.solution_text:
The distance walked is a length only, with no direction.
It is a **scalar**.

foundation.question_text: At the end of the day the same hiker is $7$ km north-east of the starting point. State whether the quantity '$7$ km north-east' is a vector or a scalar.
foundation.solution_text:
The quantity gives a size, $7$ km, and a direction, north-east.
It is a **vector**.

foundation.question_text: The vector $\underset{\sim}{p}$ represents a push on a trolley. Write, in symbols, the magnitude of $\underset{\sim}{p}$.
foundation.solution_text:
The magnitude is written with vertical bars around the vector.
$|\underset{\sim}{p}|$

The arrow starts at $M$ and its head is at $N$, so the letters are read in that order.
$\overrightarrow{MN}$

foundation.question_text: Explain why $\underset{\sim}{a}+5$ is not a meaningful expression.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{a}$ is a vector and $5$ is a scalar.
A scalar cannot be added to a vector, because $5$ carries no direction, so the sum has no meaning.
It is the vector whose magnitude is the length of the line segment from $R$ to $S$, and whose direction is from $R$ towards $S$.

foundation.question_text: A worker pushes a crate with a force of $30$ N towards the east. State whether this is a vector or a scalar quantity, and give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
The quantity gives a size, $30$ N, and a direction, east.
It is a **vector**.

The tail of the arrow is at $B$ and the head is at $A$, so the first letter is $B$.
$\overrightarrow{BA}$

development.question_text: Three of the quantities below are scalars: mass, distance, weight, area. Name the odd one out and give a reason.
development.solution_text:
Weight is the force of gravity on an object, and that force acts downwards.
Weight is the odd one out, because it is a **vector**.

development.question_text: A lift descends at $2$ m/s. Explain why this describes a vector quantity.
development.solution_text:
The size is $2$ m/s and the word 'descends' fixes the direction as downwards.
Both a magnitude and a direction are given, so it is a **vector**.

development.question_text: Explain why $7\underset{\sim}{a}$ is meaningful but $\underset{\sim}{a}+7$ is not.
development.solution_text:
$7\underset{\sim}{a}$ multiplies the vector $\underset{\sim}{a}$ by the scalar $7$, which stretches its magnitude and keeps its direction.
$\underset{\sim}{a}+7$ tries to add a scalar to a vector, and a number with no direction cannot be added to a directed quantity.

development.question_text: $|\overrightarrow{AB}|=9$ cm. Write down $|\overrightarrow{BA}|$, and give a reason.
development.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{BA}$ joins the same two points, so it has the same length.
$|\overrightarrow{BA}|=9$ cm

The left arrow runs from $C$ to $D$, and the right arrow runs from $F$ to $E$.
$\overrightarrow{CD}$ and $\overrightarrow{FE}$

$\overrightarrow{PQ}$ is a vector: it carries both the length of $PQ$ and the direction from $P$ to $Q$.
$|\overrightarrow{PQ}|$ is a scalar: it is the length of $PQ$ only, with the direction discarded.

development.question_text: A runner's average speed is $13$ km/h, and her average velocity is $13$ km/h due north. State which of these two quantities is a vector, and why.
development.solution_text:
Both quantities give the same size, $13$ km/h, but only the velocity states a direction.
The velocity is the **vector**; the speed is a scalar.

development.question_text: A student writes $|\underset{\sim}{b}|=-3$. Explain why this statement cannot be true.
development.solution_text:
$|\underset{\sim}{b}|$ is the magnitude of $\underset{\sim}{b}$, which is the length of the arrow representing it.
A length cannot be negative, so a magnitude is never negative.

development.question_text: One of the quantities temperature, force, displacement and acceleration is not a vector. Name it and give a reason.
development.solution_text:
A temperature is a reading on a scale, and no direction can be attached to it.
Temperature is the odd one out, because it is a **scalar**.

mastery.question_text: A drone flies $500$ m east, then $200$ m west along the same line. Write down the total distance it has flown and the displacement from its starting point, and state which of the two is a vector.
mastery.solution_text:
$500+200$
$=700$ m of track flown, so the distance travelled is $700$ m.
$500-200$
$=300$, so the displacement is $300$ m east.
The displacement is the **vector**, because it carries a direction; the distance is a scalar.

mastery.question_text: A ship sails from $A$ to $B$, a distance of $18$ km on a bearing of $070^{\circ}$. Write down $|\overrightarrow{BA}|$ and describe the direction of $\overrightarrow{BA}$ as a bearing.
mastery.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{BA}$ joins the same two points, so it has the same magnitude.
$|\overrightarrow{BA}|=18$ km
Its direction is the reverse of the bearing $070^{\circ}$.
$070^{\circ}+180^{\circ}$
$=250^{\circ}$, so $\overrightarrow{BA}$ points on a bearing of $250^{\circ}$.

mastery.question_text: Sort these three quantities into vectors and scalars, giving a reason for each: a pressure of $101$ kPa, a wind of $25$ knots blowing from the south-west, an area of $3$ hectares.
mastery.solution_text:
A pressure of $101$ kPa is a size only, so it is a scalar.
An area of $3$ hectares is a size only, so it is a scalar.
A wind of $25$ knots from the south-west gives a size and a direction, so it is a **vector**.
